subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Possibility Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The Possibility Effect.

hook.text: Going from 0% to 5% feels enormous. Going from 5% to 10% feels small. We overweight the jump from impossible.

buildup.text: The possibility effect: a small chance of something great (or terrible) captivates attention beyond its probability.

discovery.text: This effect drives both lottery dreams and terrorism fears. A tiny chance of extreme outcomes warps decisions.

twist.text: Insurance companies profit from this. We overpay to protect against rare catastrophes because we overweight them.

climax.text: The possibility and certainty effects are two sides of the same coin: we warp probabilities near the extremes.

punchline.text: Possible and probable feel the same. They're not.

quiz.question: What does the possibility effect cause?
options: We overweight the jump from impossible to possible

details.summary: The possibility effect occurs when people overweight small probabilities, treating unlikely events as far more probable than they actually are. A 1 percent chance of winning feels much larger than 1 percent, driving lottery purchases and excessive worry.
details.whyItMatters: The possibility effect explains irrational fear of extremely unlikely events like plane crashes and irrational hope in extremely unlikely gains like lottery wins. It profoundly distorts risk perception in everyday decisions.
takeaways: Small probabilities are psychologically inflated far beyond their actual weight
The possibility effect drives both excessive fear and excessive hope
Moving from impossible to merely improbable has outsized psychological impact

faq.question: Why does a 1 percent chance feel much larger than 1 percent?
faq.answer: The vivid imagery of the outcome, whether winning millions or dying in a crash, captures attention. Our brains process the possibility of the outcome rather than its probability, making even tiny chances of dramatic events feel significant.

faq.question: How do casinos exploit the possibility effect?
faq.answer: Casinos prominently display rare jackpot winners, making the possibility vivid. Flashing lights and sounds when anyone wins any amount reinforce the feeling that winning is possible. The actual probabilities are hidden behind the emotional experience.
